rows.figure: 2 deaths of UK fishing vessel crew
rows.scope: Deaths of crew of UK-registered commercial fishing vessels (registered with the MCA Registry of Shipping and Seamen), worldwide, from accidents reported to the MAIB, counted by the year the incident was reported. rows.figure: 11 persons fatally injured in marine accidents reported to the TSB
rows.scope: Persons fatally injured (missing persons included) in marine accidents reported to the TSB in the calendar year: 'shipping accidents' (sinking, capsize, collision, fire, grounding, damage, missing) plus 'accidents aboard ship' (boarding, on board, overboard, contact with the ship). Commercial vessels only ('registered or licensed to operate commercially'); pleasure craft occurrences 'not normally included unless they also involved a commercial vessel'. Foreign-flag vessels in Canadian waters counted. No crew/passenger split printed. Live database; figures may change.

rows.figure: 3 operational-related fatalities on domestic commercial vessels (3 fatal marine incidents)
rows.scope: Operational-related fatalities in marine incidents involving a domestic commercial vessel (DCV) reported to AMSA in the calendar year (Table 1). corrections.new: The largest unmeasured piece of the toll. No global series, but three national accident-investigation series exist for commercial vessels: UK MAIB annual reports (fishing crew, merchant crew and passenger deaths), Canada TSB marine statistical summaries (persons fatally injured, commercial vessels) and Australia AMSA marine incident annual reports (operational-related DCV fatalities): see the uk-maib-*, canada-tsb-* and australia-amsa-* rows. All exclude recreational craft except where a commercial vessel was involved; none is a drowning count.

tried: MAIB Annual Report 2024 PDF (assets.publishing.service.gov.uk, 94 pages): WebFetch text extraction ends at 107,325 characters, mid-title of Table 19 (p. 74), even with offsets; Tables 19-24 of the 2024 edition (including the 2015-2024 fishing-crew-by-length table with deaths and the non-UK vessels in UK waters table) and Annexes A and B were unreachable. The 2023 edition (99,134 characters, complete to p. 65) was used instead for the fishing-crew series 2020-2023 and for the Annex A and B definitions.
gov.uk publication page for MAIB Annual Report 2024: PDF only; no HTML version, accessible version or data tables are offered (an accessible copy must be requested by email).

gov.uk collection 'MAIB annual reports' (opened 2026-10-21) lists the 2024 report (17 July 2025) as the most recent; https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/maib-annual-report-2025 returned a fetch error, so the 2025 edition appears unpublished. UK rows therefore stop at 2024.

MAIB prints no all-vessel annual total of deaths and no multi-year table of pleasure craft deaths in the reachable text of either edition: pleasure craft deaths appear only in the 2024 and 2023 'Table 1: Loss of life reported to the MAIB' event lists, which print no total, so none was counted.

https://www.tsb.gc.ca/ home page returned a fetch error; the monthly statistics page https://tsb.gc.ca/eng/stats/marine/2024/06/index.html returned link text without URLs. The 2025 statistical summary was reached by applying the 2024 URL pattern (https://bst-tsb.gc.ca/eng/stats/marine/2025/ssem-ssmo-2025.html and the 2026-06 PDF) and confirmed by its own title and 'Data extracted 30 March 2026'.

ATSB 'Australian shipping occurrence statistics': the only editions found cover 2005 to 2012 (atsb.gov.au/node/2218 and node/2192), so not a current series; not opened. AMSA's marine incident annual reports are the current Australian source.

AMSA 2024 PDF: WebFetch reported Table A7 (fatalities by vessel class) with a Total column (4, 3, 0, 3, 4) in one pass and without a Total column in another; the 2025 PDF's Table A6 rows came back with blank cells of uncertain column alignment. Only Table 1 totals are used in the rows. Neither AMSA PDF exposes page numbers in the text extraction; the 2024 contents list places the DCV Fatalities section at p. 8 and Tables A6/A7 at p. 34.
AMSA 2024 and 2025 reports do not define 'operational-related' or state whether natural-cause deaths are excluded; the AMSA website's list of definitions referred to in the Overview was not opened.

The shared WebSearch budget was exhausted after the ATSB search, so later documents (TSB 2025 edition, AMSA 2025 edition, MAIB collection page) were reached by following links from already-opened pages or by URL pattern rather than by search.
notes: Status done for the three named sources, with caveats. Latest five years found: UK (MAIB) 2020-2024, Canada (TSB) 2021-2025, Australia (AMSA) 2021-2025. Counting rules differ and none of the three series is a boating or drowning toll: MAIB counts deaths on UK-registered commercial vessels by vessel class and role (fishing crew; merchant >=100gt crew; passengers), by year reported, with no all-vessel total printed; TSB counts persons fatally injured (including missing) in accidents involving commercial vessels, pleasure craft excluded unless a commercial vessel was involved; AMSA counts operational-related fatalities on domestic commercial vessels (crew, passengers, one rescued person), with foreign-flagged and regulated Australian vessel fatalities reported separately (1 in 2024, 0 in 2025) and recreational craft outside its reporting. The UK rows are three parallel series (15 rows) because MAIB prints no all-vessel total; the lab must not add them. Deaths on UK merchant vessels under 100gt (Table 14: 2 in 2024; 3 in 2023 per the 2023 edition, p. 52) and on non-UK commercial vessels in UK waters (2023 edition Table 24, p. 61: 4) are printed only as single-year tables and are left in notes, not rows. Revisions: the MAIB 2024 edition revised 2023 merchant crew deaths from 1 to 2 and 2023 passenger deaths from 2 to 3 (both editions' values recorded in the row notes); the TSB 2025 edition kept the 2024 total at 12 but moved one death from 'accidents aboard ship' to 'shipping accidents' (8/4 became 9/3). The UK fishing-crew values for 2020-2023 come from the 2023 edition (Table 22, p. 60) because the 2024 edition's Table 22 lies beyond the reachable text; the 2024 value (2) is from the 2024 edition's section text (p. 71) and Chief Inspector's statement (p. 2). What a person with a browser should check: (1) MAIB Annual Report 2024 pp. 74-94, Table 22 (2015-2024) for the fishing-crew deaths series and any revision of 2020-2023, plus Annex A for the 2024 coverage wording; (2) AMSA 2025 PDF page numbers for Table 1 and Table A6; (3) whether the UK merchant >=100gt crew and passenger tables include non-UK vessels carrying passengers to or from UK ports (Annex A of the 2024 edition). The TSB PDF quotes are from the 2026-06 PDF; the HTML edition carries the same tables with 'Data extracted 30 March 2026'. The US series already in the ledger (uscg-boating-2024, uscg-bard) is the only one of the four countries that covers recreational boating; no correction to uscg-bard is proposed. One correction is proposed to the note of water-transport-other to point at these national series; its figure ('No global yearly series') remains correct.
